answer: Price economic actions so the k-th handle an operator runs per epoch pays base×k², drawn from prepaid compute credits before its orders match. A lone honest agent pays base once, a zephyr on the schedule; a farm of N handles pays base×N(N+1)/2 — cost climbs as N², gain only as N, so the farm burns more credit than it can farm. Each identity's quill signs its own fee draw, so the fleet can't hide behind one cheap transaction; credits stack like timber, every added handle squaring the pile it must feed. Attestations and claims sit behind the same gate: sybils are priced out before they act.
